title: GitLab Duo Expands Self-Hosted AI Options Through Microsoft Foundry
gist: GitLab extended GitLab Duo Self-Hosted to run models via Microsoft Foundry inside a customer's own Azure environment, letting enterprises pick OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, or Mistral models per feature while keeping data-path control -- trading convenience for infrastructure responsibility, and reinforcing GitLab's positioning as a model-agnostic DevSecOps control layer rather than a model vendor.

insights.claim: GitLab Duo Self-Hosted now supports models deployed through Microsoft Foundry within an organization's own Azure environment, covering OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, and Mistral model families.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Enterprises evaluating AI coding assistants now have a path to keep model choice, deployment location, and data path entirely within their own cloud tenancy rather than a vendor-managed one.
insights.quote: The integration supports model families including OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, and Mistral, giving enterprises more choice over model provider, deployment location, and data path.

insights.claim: The architecture consists of three components -- a self-managed GitLab instance, a self-hosted GitLab AI Gateway, and model endpoints hosted through Microsoft Foundry -- with the gateway acting as an intermediary that decouples individual Duo features from any single model provider.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: The gateway layer is the reusable abstraction that lets GitLab swap or diversify model providers over time without re-architecting Duo itself.
insights.locator: The architecture consists of three main components

insights.claim: GitLab Duo supports feature-level model selection, so organizations can assign a code-focused model to Code Suggestions, a different model to agentic workloads, and a smaller model to higher-volume tasks, and can change these deployments without altering the underlying GitLab workflow.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Per-feature model routing lets enterprises optimize cost versus quality task-by-task, which pressures foundation-model vendors on price for commodity, high-volume coding tasks while reserving premium models for complex agentic work.
insights.locator: An important aspect of the integration is feature-level model selection

insights.claim: Self-hosting AI models shifts operational responsibility onto the customer's own engineering and platform teams, who must manage model deployment, capacity, networking, credentials, availability, and lifecycle in addition to the GitLab environment itself.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: The control gained from self-hosting comes with a real staffing and operations cost that buyers should weigh against the convenience of a vendor-managed AI service.
insights.quote: it shifts more responsibility onto engineering and platform teams
insights.locator: The approach also highlights an important trade-off with self-hosted AI

insights.claim: Model availability in Microsoft Foundry's catalogue does not automatically equal GitLab Duo compatibility, because Foundry's catalogue can change faster than GitLab's supported-model matrix, requiring organizations to verify compatibility across both platforms before selecting a model.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Teams standardizing on this architecture need an ongoing compatibility-verification process, not a one-time setup, to avoid silently unsupported model deployments.
insights.locator: It also means that model availability does not automatically equal GitLab Duo compatibility

insights.claim: GitHub Copilot is increasingly adding support for multiple underlying models, but its standard experience remains closely tied to GitHub's own managed service, whereas GitLab's self-hosted approach puts more emphasis on customer control of the AI infrastructure and network path.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: This is a differentiation angle for GitLab versus GitHub Copilot specifically among regulated or sovereignty-sensitive enterprise buyers who need infrastructure-level control rather than just model choice.
insights.locator: There are similarities with other enterprise development platforms

insights.claim: Multi-model infrastructure platforms such as Amazon Bedrock and Microsoft Foundry are not themselves substitutes for an integrated DevSecOps platform like GitLab, since they provide model hosting rather than the development workflow layer built around it.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Suggests DevSecOps platforms and model-hosting infrastructure occupy complementary rather than competing layers, meaning GitLab can retain its workflow moat even as the model layer underneath it commoditizes.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, platforms such as Amazon Bedrock and Microsoft Foundry

themes.theme: AI governance as a procurement dimension

insights.claim: As AI becomes embedded deeper into software engineering, enterprises increasingly must decide not just which AI capabilities developers use but where the models run, where source code and prompts travel, who controls the credentials, and which jurisdictions process the data.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: AI-tool procurement is expanding from a feature checklist into a data-governance and jurisdictional-risk decision, favoring vendors that offer deployment-location and credential control.
insights.quote: enterprises increasingly need to make decisions not just about which AI capabilities developers use, but where the models run, where source code and prompts travel, who controls the credentials, and which jurisdictions process the data.
insights.locator: The significance of the announcement therefore extends beyond another model integration

insights.claim: The development environment is increasingly resembling a model-agnostic control layer, where GitLab manages the developer workflow and AI features while the organization determines which models sit underneath.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Positions GitLab's durable value as the orchestration and workflow layer rather than any specific model partnership, a framework useful for assessing which DevSecOps vendors are insulated from foundation-model churn.
insights.quote: This makes the development environment increasingly resemble a model-agnostic control layer
insights.locator: This makes the development environment increasingly resemble a model-agnostic control layer
